title: How Sleep Supports Teenagers
text:
Sleep supports how well teenagers function each day by affecting their brains, emotions, and bodies.

During sleep, the brain organizes information from the day and prepares for the next one. Poor sleep can make it harder to remember information, pay attention, solve problems, and make decisions. Teenagers may also feel sluggish or make more mistakes when they have not slept enough.

Sleep also affects emotional health. Poor sleep can make stress, anxiety, irritability, frustration, and low mood feel stronger. When people are rested, they may be better able to manage their reactions and cope with difficult feelings.

Physical health is affected too. Poor sleep is linked with problems involving hunger, appetite, and eating habits. The body also repairs itself during sleep, and too little sleep can weaken the immune system and make it harder to fight illness.
